text.en:
Divya stirred hot dal with a steel spoon and the handle became hot. Above the pot she saw steam rising. Standing a little away she still felt warmth from the stove.
"Heat reaches me in three different ways!" she said.

Conduction is the transfer of heat through a solid from the hot part to the colder part, without the material itself moving. A steel spoon heats up this way. Metals conduct well; wood and plastic do not.
Convection is the transfer of heat by the movement of a liquid or gas. Warm fluid rises and cooler fluid sinks, making a circulation. Boiling water and sea breezes are examples.
Radiation is the transfer of heat without any material, as waves. Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth by radiation. Dark surfaces absorb more heat and light surfaces reflect it.
Conduction is heat travelling through a solid, like along a steel spoon.
Convection is heat carried by moving liquids or gases. Warm fluid rises, cool fluid sinks.
Radiation is heat travelling as waves without any material. The Sun's heat reaches us this way.
Dark surfaces take in more heat. Light surfaces reflect it.

problem.en: How does heat from the Sun reach the Earth through empty space?

text.en: Space has almost no matter, so conduction and convection cannot work.
Radiation does not need a material.
So the Sun's heat reaches us by radiation.

prompt.en: A friend says white clothes are worn in summer because they look nice. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: White reflects more heat and light and stays cooler.

commonMisconceptions.en: Missing the science behind colour choices.

points.en: Convection: through moving liquids and gases.
Radiation: as waves, with no material needed.
